privacy.google.body: When someone signs in with Google, Google sends Elifba the account holder's name and e-mail address. When the account is created, this name and address are written to it (the name can be changed later). Apart from that, Elifba keeps only the Google account's number, to recognise the account next time. No picture or other information is kept. Nothing about the children is ever sent to Google. Signing in with Google is a choice: signing up with an e-mail address and a password works too.

privacy.home.delete: A parent can delete a child on the child's page: the name, the avatar, the games and the stars are deleted at once and for good. There is no archive. Deleting the account in Settings → Profile deletes the children too.

privacy.home.not_shared: Children are never compared: there is no ranking, place or picture to share. A parent's child and a teacher's student are never linked — even for the same child they are separate records, and a teacher never sees what was played at home.
privacy.home.stored:
Parent: the account's details (name, email address, a hash of the password, the interface language) and when the parent's agreement was given.
Child: a first name only (no surname), an animal avatar, the parent's order and the learned letters. At most :max children.
Games: which game was played when, which rounds were solved and the stars earned.
A child's surname, photo, date of birth, age, gender, school or contact details are never stored.
privacy.home.title: At home: parents and their children
privacy.home.who: Only the parent's own account sees a child's name and stars; the name is shown only on the board of that parent's game.
privacy.home.why: A parent adds their own children, because the parent is the one who may decide for them. The name and the avatar show who is playing on the board, and the stars show the child's own progress.
privacy.how_long.body: Classes and students are kept until the teacher deletes them. Archived classes and students are deleted automatically after :days days, and games older than :days days are deleted with their points.

privacy.intro: Elifba helps teachers run reading games in class, and parents play reading and picture games with their own children at home. Children never use the app themselves and have no accounts. Only what the games need to work is stored.
privacy.not_stored.body: No child's photo, birth date, gender, address, phone number or ID number is stored. A student's surname and patronymic are stored only when the teacher writes them with the name, and never appear on the shared picture; for a child a parent adds, only the first name is stored. The pasted list itself is not stored. Children never log in and are never asked for anything.
privacy.not_stored.title: What is not stored

privacy.parents.description: Before you use Elifba with your class, you can copy this text and send it to parents.
privacy.parents.note:
Dear parents,

In our lessons we will use Elifba reading games to help the children learn to read. The children play on the classroom board; they never log in to the app or type anything into it.

For each child, Elifba keeps the name as I write it (with a surname and patronymic if I write them) and an animal avatar. No photo or contact details are stored; a shared picture shows only the first name. Game points are only for encouragement within the class. If a child's first name is in Elifba's name list, the board may say it with the praise in a prerecorded voice; the name is sent nowhere.

The data is deleted automatically after :days days, and you can ask me at any time to delete your child's data sooner. We use Elifba with the school's permission.

If you have any questions, please write to me.
privacy.parents.selected: The text is selected — press Ctrl+C (⌘+C on a Mac) to copy it.
privacy.parents.title: A note for a class's parents
privacy.rooms.camera: Scanning the code with the camera is optional: the browser asks first, and the picture is used only on the phone itself to find the QR code; it is sent nowhere and is not kept.
privacy.rooms.contact: Elifba asks no one's age, and there is no way for players to write to each other: no message, chat or invitation is sent. During a game a player can throw another player in the room only a taunt from a ready-made list — an emoji with a short phrase; each costs the thrower 1 point, and only the player it is aimed at and the host's big screen see it, and hear it in a prerecorded voice, for a few seconds. Anyone can hide taunts on their own device, and the host can switch them off for the room. People pass a room's code to each other outside Elifba. The host can remove any player; a removed player cannot come back to that room, and their name is no longer shown in it.
privacy.rooms.contact_voice: Elifba asks no one's age, and there is no way for players to write to each other: no message, chat or invitation is sent. During a game a player can throw another player in the room only a taunt from a ready-made list — an emoji with a short phrase; each costs the thrower 1 point, and only the player it is aimed at and the host's big screen see it, for 4 seconds. Anyone can hide taunts on their own device, and the host can switch them off for the room. Players can talk to each other only in the live voice the host turns on (below). People pass a room's code to each other outside Elifba. The host can remove any player; a removed player cannot come back to that room, their name is no longer shown in it, and they are cut from the live voice at once.
privacy.rooms.delete: In a closed room, a player can take their name out with “Remove my name”: their points stay under “Player”, so nobody else's place moves. The host can delete a closed room for everyone with “Delete the room”. Deleting the account in Settings → Profile deletes the rooms it opened too, and leaves its name in no other room. Everything else is deleted automatically after :days days.
privacy.rooms.how_long: A code works only while its room is open: the room closes and its code is cleared when the host closes it or after :hours hours with nothing happening in it. The players of a closed room still see its results with names. A room is deleted automatically with its games and answers :days days after it was opened.
privacy.rooms.intro: On this instance, adults with an Elifba account can also race each other at memory, logic and word games in rooms; what is kept for that is in the section “Games for adults” below.
privacy.rooms.live_voice:
The live voice starts on in every room; the host can turn it off and on again at any moment. Before you first join it you are asked to agree, and the moment you agreed is kept with your account; from then on you join it automatically, as a listener, in a room whose voice is on. “Leave the voice” takes you out of that room's voice, and on that device you stay out until you join again yourself: the game plays the same without it.
The microphone starts off and only the player turns it on; if it was on when you reload the page, it stays on. The browser asks for permission the first time it is turned on. From then until you leave the voice the page keeps the microphone: the browser does not ask again on that page, and the device's microphone indicator stays on meanwhile; while the microphone is off, no sound is sent. While your microphone is on, the players of that room who joined the voice, and its host, hear you live — and nobody else. The host can mute any player. A player who comes into the room while a game is running hears nothing and can say nothing until the host lets them into the voice; one who comes between games is let in at once.
The voice is not recorded, not turned into text and not kept: the voice server only passes it on to the other players at that moment. The big screen neither plays the voice nor listens. Nobody, Elifba included, can listen later to what was said; that is why only the host keeps order in a room.
The voice travels encrypted from the phone to this instance's own voice server and from there to the other players. It passes through no outside service, and the phones do not connect to each other directly, so players do not see each other's IP address. There is no end-to-end encryption: whoever runs the server could technically get access to the live voice, as with any call server.
This is all that is kept for the live voice: with the account, the moment it agreed; with the room, whether its voice is on, and whom the host let into the voice and whom the host muted. The voice server sees your IP address in order to connect; its log holds only technical lines — the moment of a connection, the random number of the room and of the player, a part of the IP address — and no name and no voice. The log has a fixed size: new lines push out old ones.
privacy.rooms.not_stored: No age, date of birth, gender, phone number, photo or nickname is asked for or stored, and nothing about a device or a location is stored for a room. A room has no name and no chat, and answers are tapped, never typed, so nothing anyone writes is stored for a room.
privacy.rooms.not_stored_voice: No age, date of birth, gender, phone number, photo or nickname is asked for or stored, and nothing about a device or a location is stored for a room. A room has no name and no chat, and answers are tapped, never typed, so nothing anyone writes is stored for a room. The live voice is not stored either: no recording, no transcript, and not who spoke or when.
privacy.rooms.share: Sending a game's link is optional. The “WhatsApp” button opens WhatsApp on the phone with a ready-made message, and “Share” opens the phone's own share sheet; the message holds one sentence and the game's link — the link holds the game's code and nobody's name. You choose whom to send it to; WhatsApp, or the app you choose, sees it and passes it on under its own rules. Elifba itself sends nothing to WhatsApp, and room pages make no requests to it. The app may open the page to build the link's preview: it sees only Elifba's name and general picture, nothing about the game. A browser that opens the link with a tap keeps the game's code in its session until registration and email confirmation are done, for an hour at most. The link stops working when the room closes.
privacy.rooms.stored:
Player: the account's details (name, email address, a hash of the password, the interface language), the “Player” role and when its agreement was given.
Room: who opened it, who joined, left or was removed and when, when each player's page last checked the room during a game (so that a round does not wait for someone who has closed the page), and which games were played at which difficulty.
Answers: in each round, what was picked, whether it was right, how long it took and the points earned.
Taunts: who threw which ready-made taunt at whom during a game, and when; whom it was aimed at is erased after a day, and the point the thrower paid stays in the game's result.
privacy.rooms.title: Games for adults
privacy.rooms.voice: At the end of a game, the host's big screen — or, in a game without the big screen, the players' phones — can say the winner's first name aloud in a prerecorded voice, if the name is in Elifba's built-in name list. The name is sent to no service and nothing is stored for it; a name that is not in the list is not said. The “Game sounds” button on the screen and on a phone silences it too.
privacy.rooms.what: An account that holds the “Player” role chooses a game: a room opens at that moment, and that account is its host. Other accounts join the room with the six-digit code the host gives them, its QR code or its link; an account that opens the link with a tap joins at once. Someone without an account who opens the link sees the registration page, where they accept the “Player” role's sentence separately from the privacy note. Everyone plays the same rounds on their own phone, and the room shows a ranking; several games can be played in one room, one after another. Rooms are for adults: a student, or a child a parent added, never takes part in one.
privacy.rooms.where: Room data is kept on this instance's own server too, and is given to no one. Room pages make no requests to outside services.
privacy.rooms.where_voice: Room data is kept on this instance's own server too, and is given to no one. The live voice also passes only through this instance's own voice server. Room pages make no requests to outside services.
privacy.rooms.who: A player's name, as the account writes it, is seen only by the hosts and the players of the rooms that player joined: on the room page, on the host's big screen and in the room's results. The name is read from the account each time: change it in Settings → Profile and it changes in every room. Nobody else sees it: there is no list of rooms or players, no search and no profile page, and a player's email address is never shown to anyone.
privacy.rooms.why: Names and points show who played how in a room and make that room's ranking. Nothing is computed outside one room: there is no total, rating, level or profile. The data is not used for advertising, analytics or anything else.
privacy.stored.body:
Teacher: name, email address, a hash of the password and the interface language.
Class: the teacher's name for it (for example “1A”), its grade and the letters it has learned.
Student: their name as the teacher writes it (with a surname and patronymic if the teacher writes them), an animal avatar and their place in the class order.
Games: which game was played when, which student solved which round, and the points they earned.
privacy.stored.title: What is stored
privacy.title: Privacy note
privacy.voice.body: The board says the prompt and the praise in a prerecorded voice. When a student's or a child's first name is in Elifba's built-in name list, the board may say it in that voice with the praise, at the start of a game at home and at the end of a game. The name is sent to no service and nothing is stored for it; a name that is not in the list is only shown in writing. It can be turned off in Settings → Games.
privacy.voice.title: The board's voice
privacy.where.body: Everything is kept on this Elifba instance's own server. Its pages make no requests to outside services: no ads, analytics, web fonts or trackers.
privacy.where.title: Where it is kept
privacy.why.body: Names and avatars show whose turn it is at the board; points make the class's daily and weekly rankings. The data is not used for advertising, analytics or anything else, and is given to no one.

welcome.meta.description: A free platform for primary-school teachers: children learn letters, syllables, words and sentences by playing on the projected classroom wall while the teacher runs the game from a phone.

welcome.privacy.wire: Pages send nothing to outside services: there are no ads, analytics or trackers.
welcome.rooms.join_text: Create an account and choose “Player”; a teacher's or a parent's account adds the role in Settings → Roles. Then choose a game and give its code to others, or join with the code you were given.
welcome.rooms.names: Players see only each other's account name. No age is asked, and there is no chat or messaging.
welcome.rooms.names_voice: Players see only each other's account name. No age is asked, and there is no chat or messaging. Players can talk live while they play, and the host can turn it off: everyone turns their own microphone on, and the voice is not recorded.

welcome.rooms.text: Adults play on Elifba too: anyone with an account can choose a game and invite friends or colleagues with its code. Everyone plays the same rounds at the same time on their own phone, and the ranking shows after every round.
